data.title: Peripheral nerve: longitudinal organisation

regions.label: Aligned wavy profiles
regions.observation: Several elongated profiles run in a similar, gently wavy direction.
regions.interpretation: This arrangement supports a longitudinal view of a nerve bundle when combined with the specimen provenance and the surrounding tissue. Follow several profiles before deciding their common axis.
regions.limit: A visible segment is not an entire axon, and the image does not distinguish sensory from motor fibres.

regions.label: Dark elongated nucleus
regions.observation: A dark, elongated nuclear profile lies among the aligned tissue profiles.
regions.interpretation: Nuclei are a useful second clue after the overall arrangement. Record the nucleus as an observation before assigning a supporting-cell identity.
regions.limit: Shape and proximity alone do not establish that this nucleus belongs to a Schwann cell rather than another cell in the tissue.

regions.label: Pale interval
regions.observation: A lighter interval separates neighbouring elongated profiles.
regions.interpretation: Preparation and separation of tissue can contribute to pale intervals. Compare its direction and continuity with surrounding fibres.
regions.limit: This isolated light interval does not demonstrate the specialised interruption of a particular myelin sheath at a node of Ranvier.

data.model: Aligned undulating fibres and elongated nuclei; field does not show an entire nerve cross-section. Do not label every nucleus as Schwann or infer a motor versus sensory axon.

introduction: Compare arrangement before naming cells. These are independent specimens, not consecutive views of one nerve. Choose a region, separate observation from interpretation, and state what this preparation cannot establish.

data.title: Peripheral nerve: transverse profiles and surrounding tissue

regions.label: Crowded transverse profiles
regions.observation: Numerous small round or oblique profiles occupy a broad grouped region.
regions.interpretation: Together with the provider identification, the arrangement supports a transverse or oblique view of fibres within a fascicular region. Compare it with the elongated profiles in the independent longitudinal specimen.
regions.limit: No calibrated scale is supplied. Do not calculate axon diameter or treat these independent images as matched sections of one nerve.

regions.label: Separation cleft
regions.observation: A pale cleft lies between the grouped profiles and more peripheral fibrous tissue.
regions.interpretation: Describe it first as a separation space. To identify a perineurial sleeve, find the continuous cellular boundary around a fascicle rather than naming the empty-looking space itself.
regions.limit: The cleft is not itself a cellular sheath. No vascular lining or contents are demonstrated here that would identify a vessel.

regions.label: Peripheral fibrous tissue
regions.observation: Fibrous-looking tissue extends outside the pale separation cleft.
regions.interpretation: Its position is useful for mapping the relationship between a fascicular region and surrounding support. The broad region can be described before resolving its individual cell layers.
regions.limit: This marker does not identify a single perineurial layer, and the displayed field is not a complete map of the entire nerve.

data.model: Many small transverse profiles within a larger fascicular region; peripheral tissue and a separation cleft are present. The separation cleft itself is not the perineurium or a vascular lumen.

introduction: Compare arrangement before naming cells. These are independent specimens, not consecutive views of one nerve. Choose a region, separate observation from interpretation, and state what this preparation cannot establish.

data.title: Peripheral nerve: documented osmium preparation

regions.label: Dark longitudinal profile
regions.observation: An elongated dark profile runs through the selected region.
regions.interpretation: The provider documents osmium-tetroxide preparation. This gives the dark contrast a preparation-specific context consistent with myelin-associated lipid.
regions.limit: The image does not resolve the molecular layers of compact myelin or quantify the amount of a myelin protein.

regions.label: Interval between profiles
regions.observation: A light interval occurs between adjacent dark profiles.
regions.interpretation: Compare continuity along each profile before interpreting the intervening space. Preparation, tissue separation and the section plane affect the appearance.
regions.limit: Lightness between profiles is not enough to identify a node or diagnose loss of myelin.

regions.label: Contrast and focus vary
regions.observation: Some profile edges are less sharp than others and contrast varies across the field.
regions.interpretation: Focus, overlap and the section plane affect what can be distinguished. Use a clearer region to formulate an anatomical claim and keep the less certain region in view as a limitation.
regions.limit: A blur or contrast change alone does not prove a developmental transition, injury or a different cell type.

data.model: Dark longitudinal fibres demonstrate a preparation chosen to contrast myelin-associated lipid. Pale interruptions and changes in focus are not all identifiable nodes of Ranvier.

introduction: Compare arrangement before naming cells. These are independent specimens, not consecutive views of one nerve. Choose a region, separate observation from interpretation, and state what this preparation cannot establish.
